Guard against the spurious index-versus-yield regression

Source: R/spurious.R
pollin_guard_spurious.Rd

A common claim regresses a dependence index against absolute yield across units (e.g. varieties). When the index is the Relative Interaction Index, (open - cage) / (open + cage), and the yield axis is the open-arm value, the open term appears on both axes, so a positive slope is partly guaranteed by construction (Pearson's 1897 spurious correlation of indices sharing a term). This guard quantifies how much of the observed slope is mechanical.

Usage

pollin_guard_spurious(open, cage, n_perm = 999L, decouple = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

open

Numeric vector of open-arm values, one per unit.

cage

Numeric vector of exclusion-arm values, one per unit.

n_perm

Number of permutations.

decouple

Optional numeric vector (one per unit) giving a yield axis that does not share a term with the index.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

An object of class pollin_spurious.

Details

The null is generated by permuting the exclusion-arm values across units while holding the open-arm values fixed: this destroys any genuine open-cage relationship but retains the shared-open coupling, so the permutation distribution of the slope is the slope expected from coupling alone. A permutation p-value near 1 means the observed slope is consistent with pure coupling – i.e. spurious. Optionally supply a decoupled yield axis (e.g. the exclusion-arm yield, or an independent vigour covariate) on which the index may be regressed without sharing a term.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# independent arms: any index~open slope here is purely mechanical
g <- pollin_guard_spurious(rpois(10, 30), rpois(10, 25),
                           n_perm = 200, seed = 1)
g
#> <pollin_spurious>  index ~ open-yield slope guard
#>   observed slope : 0.0178
#>   coupling null  : mean 0.0169, sd 0.0040 (n_perm = 200)
#>   permutation p  : 0.438  -> slope consistent with mechanical coupling (SPURIOUS risk)
